# AI Philosophers

> Free, open-source set of 36 philosopher personas for Claude Code and OpenClaw. Each persona is a SKILL.md prompt that makes the agent answer in a specific philosopher's voice, argue from their documented positions, cite their real works, and stay within what they could have known. MIT licensed.

Install in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add BhackerJ/ai-philosophers` then `/plugin install philosophers@ai-philosophers`, or clone the repo and run `bash install.sh`. On OpenClaw: `clawhub install philosopher-pack`. Repository: https://github.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/README.md): install, full list of philosophers, usage examples, FAQ
- [Plugin marketplace manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json): Claude Code plugin definition
- [OpenClaw switchboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/philosopher-pack/SKILL.md): the /philosophers skill that loads any persona on demand

## Philosophers

- [/aquinas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/aquinas/SKILL.md): Chat with Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), Italian Dominican friar and scholastic philosopher. Systematic, patient, synthesizing faith and reason.
- [/aristotle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/aristotle/SKILL.md): Chat with Aristotle (384–322 BC), Greek philosopher, student of Plato, tutor of Alexander the Great. The systematizer of knowledge: logic, ethics, politics, biology, metaphysics.
- [/buddha](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/buddha/SKILL.md): Chat with Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha (563-483 BC), founder of Buddhism. The Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path, impermanence, and the end of suffering.
- [/camus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/camus/SKILL.md): Chat with Albert Camus (1913–1960), French-Algerian philosopher of absurdism, revolt, and Mediterranean life. Clear, luminous, refuses both nihilism and false hope.
- [/confucius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/confucius/SKILL.md): Chat with Confucius (551-479 BC), founder of Confucianism. Ren (benevolence), li (ritual propriety), and the cultivation of virtue in self and society.
- [/descartes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/descartes/SKILL.md): Chat with René Descartes (1596–1650), French philosopher and mathematician. "Cogito, ergo sum" (I think, therefore I am). Dualism, method of doubt, and the foundation of modern philosophy.
- [/epicurus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/epicurus/SKILL.md): Chat with Epicurus (341–270 BC), Greek philosopher of pleasure, friendship, and the simple life. Warm, anti-fear, deeply practical.
- [/foucault](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/foucault/SKILL.md): Chat with Michel Foucault (1926–1984), French philosopher of power/knowledge, genealogy, and discipline. Analytical, subversive, historically precise.
- [/hanfeizi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/hanfeizi/SKILL.md): Chat with Han Feizi (280–233 BC), Chinese Legalist philosopher of law, technique, and power. Cold, realpolitik, unsparing.
- [/hegel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/hegel/SKILL.md): Chat with G.W.F. Hegel (1770–1831), German philosopher of dialectics, Absolute Spirit, and the philosophy of history. Notoriously dense but profoundly systematic.
- [/heidegger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/heidegger/SKILL.md): Chat with Martin Heidegger (1889–1976), German philosopher of Being, Dasein, and authenticity. Dense, neologism-heavy, world-disclosing.
- [/hobbes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/hobbes/SKILL.md): Chat with Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679), English materialist philosopher. State of nature, the Leviathan, and the war of all against all.
- [/hume](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/hume/SKILL.md): Chat with David Hume (1711–1776), Scottish empiricist philosopher. Skepticism about causation, induction, and personal identity. Naturalism and custom.
- [/kant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/kant/SKILL.md): Chat with Immanuel Kant (1724–1804), Prussian philosopher who unified rationalism and empiricism. Author of the Categorical Imperative and the Critique of Pure Reason.
- [/kierkegaard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/kierkegaard/SKILL.md): Chat with Søren Kierkegaard (1813–1855), Danish philosopher of existentialism, the leap of faith, and the individual before God. Ironic, indirect, passionately personal.
- [/laozi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/laozi/SKILL.md): Chat with Laozi (老子, 6th–4th c. BC), legendary author of the Tao Te Ching. The Tao that can be named is not the eternal Tao. Wu wei, naturalness, and the mystery of being.
- [/leibniz](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/leibniz/SKILL.md): Chat with Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716), German polymath philosopher and mathematician. Monads, pre-established harmony, principle of sufficient reason, and optimism.
- [/locke](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/locke/SKILL.md): Chat with John Locke (1632–1704), English philosopher and physician. Empiricism, natural rights, social contract, and the mind as a blank slate.
- [/marcus_aurelius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/marcus_aurelius/SKILL.md): Chat with Marcus Aurelius (121–180 AD), Roman Emperor and Stoic philosopher. Reflective, self-admonishing, deeply practical.
- [/marx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/marx/SKILL.md): Chat with Karl Marx (1818–1883), German philosopher of historical materialism, class struggle, and capitalism's contradictions. Polemical, analytical, revolutionary.
- [/mencius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/mencius/SKILL.md): Chat with Mencius (372-289 BC), Confucian philosopher who argued human nature is inherently good. The four sprouts of virtue, the benevolent ruler, and moral self-cultivation.
- [/mill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/mill/SKILL.md): Chat with John Stuart Mill (1806–1873), English philosopher of utilitarianism, liberty, and women's rights. Clear, measured, liberal.
- [/mozi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/mozi/SKILL.md): Chat with Mozi / Mo Di (470–391 BC), founder of Mohism. Universal love, anti-war, utilitarian, anti-Confucian ritual. Plain, argumentative.
- [/nagarjuna](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/nagarjuna/SKILL.md): Chat with Nagarjuna (150-250 CE), founder of Madhyamaka Buddhist philosophy. Sunyata (emptiness), the two truths, and the middle way between existence and non-existence.
- [/nietzsche](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/nietzsche/SKILL.md): Chat with Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900), German philosopher of will to power, eternal recurrence, and the Übermensch. Provocative, aphoristic, intensely poetic.
- [/plato](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/plato/SKILL.md): Chat with Plato (428–348 BC), Athenian philosopher, student of Socrates, founder of the Academy. He explores the eternal Forms, the ideal city, love, and the immortal soul.
- [/rousseau](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/rousseau/SKILL.md): Chat with Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712–1778), Swiss-French philosopher of the social contract, natural goodness, and education. Passionate, personal, contradictory.
- [/sartre](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/sartre/SKILL.md): Chat with Jean-Paul Sartre (1905–1980), French existentialist philosopher. Existence precedes essence. Radical freedom, bad faith, and commitment.
- [/schopenhauer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/schopenhauer/SKILL.md): Chat with Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860), German philosopher of will, pessimism, and aesthetic redemption. Sardonic, brilliant, contemptuous of optimists and Hegel.
- [/shankara](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/shankara/SKILL.md): Chat with Adi Shankaracharya (788–820 AD), Indian philosopher of Advaita Vedanta. Non-dualism, Brahman=Atman, maya. Precise, mystical, debate-ready.
- [/socrates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/socrates/SKILL.md): Chat with Socrates (469–399 BC), Athenian philosopher who invented the dialectical method. He claims to know nothing, yet draws out truth through relentless questioning.
- [/spinoza](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/spinoza/SKILL.md): Chat with Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677), Dutch philosopher of reason and necessity. Pantheism, determinism, and the intellectual love of God. "God, or Nature."
- [/wang_yangming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/wang_yangming/SKILL.md): Chat with Wang Yangming (1472–1529), Neo-Confucian philosopher of innate moral knowledge and the unity of knowledge and action. Dynamic, experiential.
- [/wittgenstein](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/wittgenstein/SKILL.md): Chat with Ludwig Wittgenstein (1889-1951), Austrian-British philosopher of language. Late Wittgenstein: language games, family resemblance, forms of life, meaning as use.
- [/xunzi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/xunzi/SKILL.md): Chat with Xunzi / Xun Kuang (310–235 BC), Confucian philosopher of ritual, education, and human nature as evil. Systematic, rigorous.
- [/zhuangzi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhackerJ/ai-philosophers/main/zhuangzi/SKILL.md): Chat with Zhuangzi (369-286 BC), Taoist philosopher of radical freedom and transformation. The butterfly dream, the cook and the ox, relativity of perspectives. Playful and profound.
